F1_s1.explanation: The unit responds to the area just below a forward-facing head where a soft, finely fibrous surface curves into a broader body mass, often with a lighter patch or a small pink protruding shape beneath the jaw line. The response is strongest when the region is lit, mid-frame and fills a moderate part of the image.

parsed.explanation: The unit responds to the area just below a forward-facing head where a soft, finely fibrous surface curves into a broader body mass, often with a lighter patch or a small pink protruding shape beneath the jaw line. The response is strongest when the region is lit, mid-frame and fills a moderate part of the image.
parsed.evidence: Nearly all top-20 boxes sit on the lower-jaw, throat or upper-chest zone of fluffy, finely textured subjects, often where pale and dark tones meet or a pinkish open-mouth shape appears. The few top images with a different subject type (#1, #6, #10) still show the same textured transition below a head, and random images without this structure score only 1-4.
parsed.missing_data: Activation maps on images that have the soft fibrous texture but no head-to-body transition, and on smooth-surfaced images that have the transition, would separate the texture contribution from the shape contribution.

F1_s2.explanation: The unit responds to the narrow region just below a forward-pointing head shape, where a face meets a neck or chest, especially when the surface there has fine, soft, hair-like texture. It responds more weakly to a glossy pink lobe hanging from an open mouth-like opening and to finely streaked versions of the same neck-region texture.

parsed.explanation: The unit responds to the narrow region just below a forward-pointing head shape, where a face meets a neck or chest, especially when the surface there has fine, soft, hair-like texture. It responds more weakly to a glossy pink lobe hanging from an open mouth-like opening and to finely streaked versions of the same neck-region texture.
parsed.evidence: Most top boxes sit on the chin, throat or upper chest under a snout-like protrusion, and several (#8, #13, #15, #18) land on a hanging pink lobe. The top-1 image shows the same placement on a streaked, speckled surface, and random images are low (1-4), with the highest being a close, front-facing head with a visible chin region (#8).
parsed.missing_data: Occlusion or crop tests isolating throat texture versus open-mouth pink regions, plus examples from the middle of the activation range, to show which cue drives the unit.
